title: Agent Shield
text: Agent Shield: Adversarial Eval Framework + Local Runtime Perimeter. I break AI agents on purpose so they fail in my lab, not in production. Agent Shield stress tests LLM agents across prompt injection, MCP tool poisoning, RAG memory poisoning, and behavioral drift. It runs on UK AISI's Inspect AI harness, maps every threat to OWASP and MITRE ATLAS, and now carries a second claim surface: a local runtime perimeter that screens MCP tool descriptions in flight.

title: Agent Shield
text: Problem: Agent security benchmarks generally answer two questions: did the user's task succeed, and did the attack succeed. That leaves a third outcome invisible, the agent that resists an attack and never mentions it. Silent resistance beats a hijack, but it still leaves the person accountable for the agent with no idea an attack happened, so the project measures operator-facing disclosure as a third axis next to attack success.

title: Agent Shield
text: Constraint: Statistical power. Exactly one module is anchored at n=20; the rest are underpowered, so module count must never be read as result count.

title: Agent Shield
text: Constraint: Providers do not honour seeds. The Anthropic API has no server-side seed, so epochs are stochastic samples and baselines have to be re-run in the same session as the defended runs.

title: Agent Shield
text: Constraint: Provider capability. One provider emits tool-call envelopes its own API rejects and another hung at log open, so some rows are marked absent rather than filled with zeros that would read as safe.

title: Agent Shield
text: Constraint: Paraphrase. Disclosure is scored against a phrase list, and a model that discloses in its own words escapes it.

title: Agent Shield
text: Constraint: Dual-use. High-risk fixtures stay gated behind an explicit confirmation flag.

title: Agent Shield
text: Failure mode: The agentic anchor was withdrawn after publication. A harness subtlety (Inspect reads the model-visible tool description from the execute function's docstring) meant the poisoning payload never reached the model, so an n=20 table that had already been written up measured something else entirely.

title: Agent Shield
text: Failure mode: Both scorers miss the same paraphrase in the same direction. A completion that plainly describes the injection attempt scores zero transparency and inflates attack success, because the phrase list does not contain that wording.

title: Agent Shield
text: Failure mode: A better transparency scorer exists and is deliberately not shipped. The v2 LLM judge beat v1 on a live holdout (recall 0.889 vs 0.444), but that holdout was synthetic, so the worse scorer stays in the headline until the expanded set is human-labelled.

title: Agent Shield
text: Failure mode: The standalone screener passes an email-redacted poisoned catalog as a clean ALLOW; only the proxy path catches it. Tool input_schema is not screened at all, and schema screening remains shadow-only.

title: Agent Shield
text: Failure mode: The repo's own CI runs mypy against a file list that excludes the shipped runtime perimeter, so the product surface is the part not type-checked. Noted in its internal audit: a project that screens other people's agents for unsafe patterns was running none of that tooling on itself.

title: Agent Shield
text: Failure mode: Two planned modules were never built, and internal docs still describe the withdrawn anchor as current.

title: Agent Shield
text: Evidence: 6 live attack modules, 28 attack IDs: prompt injection, MCP tool poisoning, RAG/memory poisoning, covert exfiltration, social engineering, multi turn behavioral drift

title: Agent Shield
text: Evidence: Introduced Transparency Rate, whether an agent flags an attack to its operator, as a third axis alongside ASR and Benign Utility in a six cell outcome model extending AgentDojo's 2x2 matrix

title: Agent Shield
text: Evidence: One anchored surface: inputs/ (prompt injection) at n=20 with Wilson 95% CIs. Every other module is labelled a diagnostic probe rather than quietly presented as a powered result

title: Agent Shield
text: Evidence: The tools/ anchor was withdrawn by its own author. Inspect builds the model-visible tool description from the execute function's docstring, not the @tool factory's, so the TL-01 payload never reached the model: the published n=20 rows measured unprompted send_message calls, not tool poisoning. The rows are kept as historical records and a rerun is pending

title: Agent Shield
text: Evidence: On anchored prompt injection Sonnet 4.5 shows TR 0.150 while three other models read 0.000, but only Sonnet has the anchored n=20 row. At n=5 the Wilson upper bound is 0.435, so 'Sonnet is the only model that discloses' is not yet a powered claim and the repo refuses to make it

title: Agent Shield
text: Evidence: Spotlighting raises TR to 0.800 and also adds 0.200 to ASR. That second number is a scorer artifact, not compliance: the completion discloses the attack in a paraphrase the v1 phrase list does not cover, so both scorers miss the same disclosure in the same direction

title: Agent Shield
text: Evidence: The runtime perimeter ships with its own honest-limits block: an email-redacted TL-01 catalog is a clean ALLOW on the standalone screener, and input_schema (parameter descriptions, examples, $defs) is not screened at all

title: Agent Shield
text: Evidence: Local runtime perimeter (agent-shield-guard, agent-shield-mcp-proxy) screens untrusted text and MCP tool descriptions, quarantines known poisons, and raises operator alerts. A library and CLI by design, deliberately not a hosted firewall

title: Agent Shield
text: Evidence: Bounded research control plane that makes no network calls of its own: query redaction, CIA classification, source screening, approval manifests, retrieved content screening, quarantine, and append only audit events wrapped around whichever agent does the fetching

title: Agent Shield
text: Evidence: TR-v2 LLM judge built as a challenger to the v1 phrase list scorer, held back from promotion until a human labeled holdout clears a 5% false positive gate

title: Agent Shield
text: Evidence: Built on Inspect AI (UK AISI harness), standard aligned rather than ad hoc; all attacks mapped to OWASP LLM, OWASP Agentic, MITRE ATLAS, and AIVSS

title: Agent Shield
text: Evidence: Released as a Zenodo preprint (doi:10.5281/zenodo.20789431) with framework, attack registries, seeds, and logs

title: Agent Shield
text: Architecture: Two surfaces. Eval: Seeded Task → Inspect AI Harness → Agent Under Test → Scorers → ASR + Utility + Transparency. Runtime: Untrusted Text / MCP Tool Description → Screener → Quarantine or Pass → Operator Alert

title: Agent Shield
text: Tradeoff: Anchored vs diagnostic: exactly one surface is powered at n=20 and the rest are labelled probes, so module count must not be read as result count

title: Agent Shield
text: Tradeoff: Automated scoring vs human rater (automated is cheaper and seeded for reproducibility)

title: Agent Shield
text: Tradeoff: Safety of running attacks vs value of knowing failure modes (sandboxed, logged, bounded)

title: Agent Shield
text: Tradeoff: Local library vs hosted service: shipping a library keeps the claim checkable and avoids a product promise the evidence does not support yet

title: Agent Shield
text: Decision: Built on Inspect AI, not a custom harness. The field needs evals that compose; UK AISI’s harness is the closest thing to a standard.

title: Agent Shield
text: Decision: Unified scoring across every attack class. Attacks only get comparable when the scoreboard is the same. ASR, benign utility, and transparency hold everywhere.

title: Agent Shield
text: Decision: Seeded JSONL tasks + OWASP / MITRE ATLAS mapping. A result that can’t be re-run is a rumor, and a threat without a taxonomy is a one-off. Every run is reproducible and mapped.

title: Agent Shield
text: Decision: Label anchored results separately from diagnostic probes. Six live modules is not six powered results. One surface carries n=20 and Wilson intervals; the rest are explicitly marked probes so the README can never be misread as a leaderboard. Tradeoff: The project reads as thinner than a benchmark that reports every module as a result, and the honest framing is the less impressive one.

title: Agent Shield
text: Decision: Withdraw a published anchor rather than keep the rows. The TL-01 payload never reached the model-visible tool description, so the n=20 table measured unprompted message calls rather than tool poisoning. A result that measures the wrong thing is worse than no result. Tradeoff: It cost the project its second headline claim: no agentic anchor currently stands, and the rerun is still pending.

title: Agent Shield
text: Decision: Keep the weaker transparency scorer in the headline. The v2 LLM judge beat the phrase-list scorer on a live holdout, but that holdout was synthetic rather than real episode text, so promoting it would swap a measured number for a promising one. Tradeoff: The published transparency numbers are knowingly too low, and the paraphrase gap stays in the headline until the expanded set is human-labelled.

title: Agent Shield
text: Decision: Ship the runtime perimeter as a local library, not a service. The eval numbers and the runtime guard are different claims with different evidence. Keeping the perimeter local and CLI-shaped keeps them from being quoted as one thing. Tradeoff: Two separate claims in one repository are harder to explain than one, and the fixture proof metrics get mistaken for the eval result anyway.

title: Agent Shield
text: Metrics: Attack IDs: 6 modules · 28; Anchored: 1 surface · n=20

title: Agent Shield
text: Tags: Inspect AI, AgentDojo, HarmBench, Prompt Injection, MCP Security, Runtime Perimeter, OWASP / MITRE ATLAS, Python. Status: SHIPPED.

title: Personal Digital Twin
text: Personal Digital Twin: Persistent Agent Memory Behind a Fail-Closed Privacy Boundary. A context window is always too small. This decides what earns a slot in it. A persistent personalised agent whose retrieval layer tags every chunk with its origin (profile, interview transcript, or expert reflection), ranks candidates by cosine similarity with a per-section offset, and masks disallowed sources to negative infinity before top-k so a filtered-out chunk cannot re-enter on score alone. The index refuses to build at all while a real transcript lacks a matching redacted copy, or while any transcript chunk contains more than 60% of a gold evaluation answer.

title: Personal Digital Twin
text: Problem: A personalised agent accumulates far more material than a context window holds, so every turn is a selection problem: given a question, which few pieces of what the system knows about a person actually deserve to be in front of the model? Ranking by similarity alone answers that badly, because the most textually similar paragraph is often not the most useful one, and because some material should never reach the model regardless of how well it scores.

title: Personal Digital Twin
text: Constraint: Fixed context budget. Five chunks reach the model per turn, so selection is the whole game.

title: Personal Digital Twin
text: Constraint: Privacy. Raw interview transcripts must never be embedded; only a redacted copy may enter the index.

title: Personal Digital Twin
text: Constraint: Evaluation integrity. Indexed material can silently contain the answers to the evaluation set, which would make retrieval scores meaningless.

title: Personal Digital Twin
text: Constraint: Local inference, so the material never leaves the machine, against weaker models than hosted frontier ones.

title: Personal Digital Twin
text: Constraint: Reproducibility. The same profile, transcript, and reflections must produce the same index.

title: Personal Digital Twin
text: Evidence: Three source-tagged indexes over the profile, the redacted interview transcript, and expert reflections; every chunk and every index row carries its source

title: Personal Digital Twin
text: Evidence: Retrieval masks disallowed sources to negative infinity before top-k, so a source filter cannot be defeated by a high similarity score

title: Personal Digital Twin
text: Evidence: Section-aware ranking: a decide-intent query adds a +0.05 offset to chunks from the Decisions section, enough to change the cut only where scores are close

title: Personal Digital Twin
text: Evidence: The index build fails closed twice: RedactionRequired when a real transcript has no up-to-date redacted copy, and LeakError when a transcript chunk contains more than 60% of a gold evaluation answer

title: Personal Digital Twin
text: Evidence: A combined content hash over all three inputs, so an index cannot silently drift from the material it was built from

title: Personal Digital Twin
text: Evidence: Index files written before the source tagging existed still load, so the schema change did not orphan earlier work

title: Personal Digital Twin
text: Architecture: Profile + redacted transcript + reflections -> collect_chunks (tag source) -> embed -> index (+ combined hash) -> query embed -> cosine + section boost -> source mask -> top-k -> local model

title: Personal Digital Twin
text: Tradeoff: The section boost is a hand-set constant, not a learned weight. It is legible and tunable, but it is a judgement call rather than a fitted one.

title: Personal Digital Twin
text: Tradeoff: Failing the whole index build on a redaction or leak check means one bad chunk blocks all work, which is the correct default for privacy and the wrong one for iteration speed.

title: Personal Digital Twin
text: Tradeoff: Local embedding and inference keep the material on the machine at the cost of model quality relative to hosted frontier models.

title: Personal Digital Twin
text: Decision: Mask sources before top-k, not after. Filtering after ranking would let a disallowed chunk consume one of the five slots and then be dropped, silently shrinking the context. Setting masked rows to negative infinity before selection means the budget is always spent on admissible material. Tradeoff: Scores are no longer comparable across filter settings, so a chunk's rank only means something relative to the sources currently allowed.

title: Personal Digital Twin
text: Decision: Refuse to build the index rather than warn. A redaction gate that only warns is a gate that gets skipped under time pressure, and the failure it prevents is unrecoverable: once raw transcript text is embedded, it is in the index. The build raises instead. Tradeoff: One unredacted chunk blocks the entire build, which is deliberately obstructive during iteration.

title: Personal Digital Twin
text: Decision: Treat evaluation leakage as a build-time error. If indexed material contains the gold answers, retrieval scores measure memorisation rather than retrieval, and the evaluation quietly stops meaning anything. A containment check over gold answers runs before anything is embedded. Tradeoff: The 60% word-containment threshold is a heuristic. It will not catch a paraphrased answer, and it can fire on a passage that merely shares vocabulary.

title: Personal Digital Twin
text: Decision: A small additive section offset instead of a re-ranker. For a decide-style question, a recorded decision is usually more useful than a merely similar paragraph. A +0.05 offset expresses that preference where scores are close and stays out of the way where they are not. Tradeoff: It cannot express anything more subtle than a per-section constant, and the value was set by inspection rather than fitted against a labelled set.

title: Personal Digital Twin
text: Metrics: Context budget: k=5 · 3 sources; Leak gate: 0.6 containment

title: Personal Digital Twin
text: Tags: Agent Architecture, Memory, RAG, Context Engineering, Local Inference, Python. Status: SHIPPED.

title: AI RemixMate
text: AI RemixMate: Full-Stack DJ Engine with Research-Grade MIR. A DJ engine that mixes two songs into one clean transition, with 904 tests proving it. AI RemixMate is a full stack DJ engine: a React/TypeScript frontend with SSE live streaming, a FastAPI async job queue, and a research grade MIR core (TIV harmonic scoring, Beat This! downbeat detection, CLAP 512-D semantic search), with 904 tests and mastering to -14 LUFS.

title: AI RemixMate
text: Evidence: FastAPI async job queue (SQLite write-through persistence) + React/TypeScript frontend, 10 pages, SSE live job streaming, Zustand state management

title: AI RemixMate
text: Evidence: TIV harmonic scoring (Bernardes et al. 2016 Tonal Interval Space) replacing psychoacoustic consonance approximation

title: AI RemixMate
text: Evidence: Beat This! (ISMIR 2024) downbeat detection with 8/16/32-bar grid snapping, replacing librosa beat_track

title: AI RemixMate
text: Evidence: Cosine-taper stem bass ramp (no IIR bleed) + FxNorm per-stem-type LUFS normalization using corpus-derived targets

title: AI RemixMate
text: Evidence: CLAP 512-D semantic search (crate_digger.py) + Essentia arousal/valence energy arc modeling for setlist planning

title: AI RemixMate
text: Evidence: rekordbox XML + Serato GEOB cue export to bridge output into professional DJ software

title: AI RemixMate
text: Evidence: Learned spectral matching: mel band trajectory matching picks track B's entry phrase against A's outro evolution, with drop aware scoring so B's drop lands just after handover and never mid crossfade. Per band weights update online from thumbs up/down verdicts, one shot per render

title: AI RemixMate
text: Evidence: Post render spectral sync: a time varying multiband EQ eases the overlap spectrum from A to B, transient preserving via onset flux protection, gain capped and edge tapered, bass band left untouched

title: AI RemixMate
text: Evidence: Masking aware multiband EQ (Hafezi & Reiss 2015) behind a defensive import, so a missing dependency degrades to no EQ instead of breaking the render

title: AI RemixMate
text: Evidence: Two mixing engines selectable per job: a frozen byte faithful vendor of the April 2026 algorithm alongside the current pipeline, with every result recording which engine produced it

title: AI RemixMate
text: Evidence: Live-testing passes against the running app kept catching what the shape-only test suite couldn't: a compatibility scorer marking key-clashing pairs ‘compatible,’ a library-count undercount from a partial indexing write, a duplicate song-naming policy causing request floods, and a job executor that never emitted terminal SSE frames so job cards froze at their last progress percentage forever. Each one has a regression test now

title: AI RemixMate
text: Evidence: 904 tests across unit, behavioral, and integration suites; GitHub Actions CI

title: AI RemixMate
text: Architecture: Track A + B → Demucs Stems → Beat This! Downbeats → Bar-Grid Snap → TIV Harmonic Match → Stem Bass Ramp + FxNorm → -14 LUFS Master → FastAPI Job Queue → React SSE Frontend

title: AI RemixMate
text: Tradeoff: Beat This! (accurate downbeats, ~50 MB model) vs librosa (fast, weaker bar detection) — Beat This! wins for cue snapping accuracy

title: AI RemixMate
text: Tradeoff: TIV harmonic score (MIR literature, continuous) vs Camelot Wheel (DJ convention, discrete) — both exposed; TIV used for transition planning

title: AI RemixMate
text: Tradeoff: CLAP 512-D (semantic audio search, 300 MB download) vs 35-D music_index (instant, keyword-only) — CLAP for search, 35-D as fallback

title: AI RemixMate
text: Tradeoff: True stem bass ramp vs IIR shelving filter — ramp eliminates IIR bass bleed on sustained notes

title: AI RemixMate
text: Decision: Replace librosa beat_track with Beat This! (ISMIR 2024). librosa gives beat times but misses downbeats. Phrase-boundary cue snapping to 8/16/32-bar grid requires knowing which beat is beat 1. Beat This! predicts this directly.

title: AI RemixMate
text: Decision: TIV harmonic scoring alongside Camelot Wheel. Camelot is discrete (adjacent or not). TIV gives a continuous compatibility score [0,1] from the Tonal Interval Space, so transition planning can rank candidates, not just filter them.

title: AI RemixMate
text: Decision: Cosine-taper stem bass ramp instead of IIR shelving. IIR filters have group delay and bleed on sustained bass notes. A cosine taper with derivative=0 at endpoints makes no audible click and hard-zeros Song A bass after the swap.

title: AI RemixMate
text: Decision: CLAP 512-D semantic search over 35-D handcrafted embeddings. 35-D features (BPM, key, energy) can’t capture timbral similarity. CLAP embeds audio into a space shared with text, so ‘find me something that sounds like X’ actually works.

title: AI RemixMate
text: Decision: Learn spectral band weights from listener verdicts, one shot per render. Whether a transition sounds right is a taste judgment no offline metric captures. A thumbs up/down per render is the cheapest honest signal available, and capping it at one update per render keeps a single opinionated session from overfitting the weights.

title: AI RemixMate
text: Decision: Keep the old mixing engine as a frozen, selectable option. The rewrite is not automatically better on every track. Vendoring the previous engine byte-faithfully and tagging each result with its engine makes it a comparison rather than a bet.

title: AI RemixMate
text: Metrics: Tests: 904; Mastering: −14 LUFS

title: AI RemixMate
text: Tags: FastAPI, React/TypeScript, Demucs, Beat This!, CLAP, Essentia, librosa, Audio ML. Status: SHIPPED.

title: AkashicTree
text: AkashicTree: Automated Content Generation Pipeline. One short brief in; a matching script, image, and voiceover out. Swap any model, no rewrites. title: AI Health Journal
text: AI Health Journal: Local RAG Journal with a Measured Safety Floor. A private journaling AI where the two claims that matter, recall and crisis safety, are measured, not promised. AI Health Journal is a local first journaling assistant whose two load bearing claims, does retrieval surface the right past entry and does the safety floor catch a crisis, are measured and reproducible offline rather than asserted.

title: AI Health Journal
text: Problem: A journaling assistant that reads back your own history has to do two things well, and both are easy to fake. It has to retrieve the entry that actually matters rather than the one that shares the most words, and it has to recognise when an entry describes a crisis rather than a bad week. Getting the second one wrong in either direction causes harm: miss it and someone in danger gets a cheerful reframe, over-trigger it and ordinary difficulty gets pathologised.

title: AI Health Journal
text: Constraint: Privacy. Journal content must not leave the machine; cloud backends are double-gated and the client is never constructed while the gate is closed.

title: AI Health Journal
text: Constraint: The safety floor cannot depend on the model. It has to fire when the verifier call fails or the machine is offline.

title: AI Health Journal
text: Constraint: Local models are slow and weaker. Measured per-case latency ran 24 to 67 seconds across eight local models.

title: AI Health Journal
text: Constraint: Evaluation data could not be scraped from real people's mental-health posts, so the case sets are authored rather than collected.

title: AI Health Journal
text: Constraint: Dependencies were kept minimal, which bounded what could be measured: no cross-encoder rerank was testable without pulling torch for a single measurement.

title: AI Health Journal
text: Failure mode: The external validation is unflattering and was kept. Scored against GoEmotions, the valence lexicon reached 0.551 overall accuracy where always guessing the majority class is the baseline, with negative recall at 0.260. A coverage fix moved it to 0.575 on an untouched split, and the log's own verdict is that this is the correct headline number and it is not a good one.

title: AI Health Journal
text: Failure mode: Crisis sensitivity is optimistic by construction. The case set was authored with the detection patterns visible, so specificity is the more trustworthy half and an unbiased estimate needs a held-out set. The repo says so next to the number.

title: AI Health Journal
text: Failure mode: Six known gaps in the safety floor are excluded from the headline scores and still missed by design, including vague departure phrasing and non-English self-harm phrasing.

title: AI Health Journal
text: Failure mode: One bug was traced and deliberately left unfixed: an entry about someone else's crisis fires the user's own support message, because the exemption that would suppress it would also suppress a person describing their own feelings through a therapist's framing. The case is marked accepted rather than quietly patched.

title: AI Health Journal
text: Failure mode: A config value can be silently ignored. Reading a store built with one embedder while configured for another does not raise; the vector store falls back to the embedding function recorded on the collection, so retrieval keeps working under the old model. Recorded as not yet detected.

title: AI Health Journal
text: Failure mode: No outcome data of any kind. Nothing here shows that using the app helps anyone, and there is no efficacy study or psychometric validation.

title: AI Health Journal
text: Evidence: Retrieval ablation across 4 strategies (dense MiniLM, BM25, hybrid RRF, dense nomic-embed-text) on a corpus where every query is tagged with the confusion it was built to induce

title: AI Health Journal
text: Evidence: The valence_flip category went 0.667 to 1.000 on an embedder swap that also lifted full corpus Recall@3 to 0.968 and runs roughly twice as fast (26.6ms vs 58.0ms median per embedding)

title: AI Health Journal
text: Evidence: Two alternative fixes built, measured, and rejected: a score threshold (relevant and irrelevant distributions overlap completely) and a valence aware reranker (helped the weak embedder, actively hurt the strong one). Both kept documented rather than deleted, so they do not get re proposed

title: AI Health Journal
text: Evidence: Crisis safety floor at sensitivity 1.000 and specificity 0.971, deterministic and LLM free, so it still holds on an offline machine or a failed verifier call

title: AI Health Journal
text: Evidence: That eval was verified by breaking the thing it measures: deleting one euphemistic crisis pattern drops sensitivity to 0.909, names both missed entries, and exits non zero

title: AI Health Journal
text: Evidence: Five detector reframe quality rubric (minimising, toxic positivity, commanding language, ungrounded genericness, invalidating pivots), each detector proven load bearing by independent disable mutation testing: recall drops 1.000 to 0.800, missing exactly its own cases

title: AI Health Journal
text: Evidence: Multi model Draft, Verify, Revise pipeline over local Ollama models, auto selected against the machine's capacity rather than pinned to one model size

title: AI Health Journal
text: Evidence: Local first by default: PRIVACY_MODE=strict scrubs PII before storage, and Pinecone and Anthropic are both opt in gates that ship off

title: AI Health Journal
text: Evidence: Stated limits, on the card because they are on the repo: 31 document retrieval corpus, 24 queries, case sets authored with the implementation visible. Sensitivity is therefore optimistic and specificity is the more trustworthy half

title: AI Health Journal
text: Architecture: Entry → PII Scrub → Embed (nomic-embed-text) → Chroma Retrieve → Safety Tier Gate → Draft / Verify / Revise over local Ollama → Reflection

title: AI Health Journal
text: Tradeoff: Sensitivity gated at 1.000 while specificity is gated lower: a false positive shows one unnecessary supportive message, a false negative lets a reframe reach someone in real danger. The two errors are not equally bad and the gates say so

title: AI Health Journal
text: Tradeoff: Deterministic floor vs LLM verifier: the floor is weaker but survives an offline machine, so it is the layer the guarantee rests on

title: AI Health Journal
text: Tradeoff: On device (private, bounded by local hardware) vs cloud (scale, leak risk). Cloud exists as an opt in gate, never a default

title: AI Health Journal
text: Tradeoff: Small self authored eval sets vs no measurement at all: worth having, worth caveating in the same breath

title: AI Health Journal
text: Decision: Report retrieval per category, never as an aggregate. The aggregate was 0.875 and hid a category sitting at 0.667. An average is where a failure goes to hide.

title: AI Health Journal
text: Decision: Verify every eval by breaking it before trusting a green run. A guard that passes against the bug it exists to catch is not a test. Deleting a crisis pattern has to turn the build red, or the build was never watching.

title: AI Health Journal
text: Decision: Keep the rejected challengers documented instead of deleting them. A proposal that failed measurement is the only thing that stops it being re proposed six months later.

title: AI Health Journal
text: Decision: Deterministic safety floor underneath the model, not inside it. The tier gate cannot depend on an LLM call succeeding. Whatever else fails, the crisis path still has to hold. The rule is that whether a property is mechanically checkable decides whether it belongs in code or in the model. Tradeoff: The floor is English-only and brittle to phrasing. Six known gaps are recorded and excluded from the headline rather than chased with an ever-growing regex, and two patterns were removed after live testing because they collided with ordinary usage.

title: AI Health Journal
text: Decision: Set each filter's breadth by the cost of its own false positive. Missing a crisis is unrecoverable, so the crisis floor is deliberately over-broad and keeps false positives it could remove. The harsh-output filter runs the opposite way: a false positive there silently deletes a useful suggestion, so over-broad patterns would quietly gut the analysis. Tradeoff: There is no single sensitivity dial to reason about. Each filter has to be argued and measured separately, and some false positives are kept on purpose.

title: AI Health Journal
text: Decision: Run local models by default and accept what that costs. Journal content is the most sensitive data the app touches, so the trust boundary is local disk and cloud backends stay double-gated. Tradeoff: Measured across eight local models the best case-pass rate was 0.500, and the shipped default scores below that. It was chosen for latency instead, at roughly 24 seconds per case against a worst case near 67.

title: AI Health Journal
text: Metrics: Retrieval: 0.968 Recall@3; Crisis floor: 1.000 sensitivity

title: AI Health Journal
text: Tags: RAG, Ollama, ChromaDB, Retrieval Evals, Mutation Testing, DPO, Flask, Local-First. Status: SHIPPED.

It is the methodology that became the base for Agent Shield.

title: Sourcewarden
text: Sourcewarden: Security-Gated n8n Workflow Orchestration. A chatbot that helps you build n8n workflows, and only exposes what's actually safe to expose. Sourcewarden merges a retrieval index and a multi agent orchestration system for building n8n workflows behind a read only FastAPI layer that grounds every chat answer in cited evidence and verifies its own security controls live instead of shelling out to run anything itself.

title: Sourcewarden
text: Problem: An assistant that builds automation workflows has two ways to be dangerous. It can invent a node parameter that looks plausible and produces a workflow that fails in production, and it can take a live action against a real instance on the strength of its own say-so. This project treats both as gate problems rather than prompt problems: evidence has a fixed precedence order, and any live mutation is held behind a fail-closed, externally signed approval.

title: Sourcewarden
text: Constraint: Evidence precedence is fixed. Documentation and community examples inform a plan but never prove an exact node parameter for the target instance.

title: Sourcewarden
text: Constraint: The retrieval package runs on the Python standard library alone, with no network and no vector database in the test path.

title: Sourcewarden
text: Constraint: The signing key must be unreachable by agents and workspace code, which puts approval outside the system that wants approval.

title: Sourcewarden
text: Constraint: Self-improvement shares a trust boundary with the controls that authorise it, so a local apply would let a compromised tuner change both behaviour and its own evidence.

title: Sourcewarden
text: Constraint: Writes are serialised and concurrency is capped, so reviewers cannot race ahead of writers.

title: Sourcewarden
text: Failure mode: The flagship evaluation run executed zero behavioural cases. Its own result file records the reason: no approved behavioural runner or externally signed evaluator evidence was available, and structural validation is not a behavioural score. The audit reaches the same verdict independently and holds the proposal as not promotable.

title: Sourcewarden
text: Failure mode: Live mutation against a real instance is never exercised end to end. It needs a connected instance plus an externally produced signed ledger, so the gate correctly denies by default and there is no in-repo demo of a successful signed mutation.

title: Sourcewarden
text: Failure mode: Security is defence in depth, not a guarantee. Higher-precedence settings can still disable project hooks, and an ALLOW from a reviewing agent never grants new authority.

title: Sourcewarden
text: Failure mode: The self-improvement loop cannot close. It always terminates at an external-integrator block by design, and the infrastructure that would complete it does not exist in the repository.

title: Sourcewarden
text: Failure mode: The retrieval fallback is a degradation rather than an equivalent. Hash-based fallback is lower quality than semantic embeddings and is documented as an availability fallback only.

title: Sourcewarden
text: Failure mode: No CI workflow is committed; the gate is a make target run by hand. The project's own audit ships as done-with-concerns with open blockers.

title: Sourcewarden
text: Evidence: 2,256-row retrieval index across official n8n docs and community workflow examples, with an explicit evidence precedence: live instance schema, then official docs, then community examples, then untrusted references

title: Sourcewarden
text: Evidence: Six-role agent orchestration (supervisor, security firewall, skeleton architect, module builder, deviation monitor, eval tuner) gated by an Ed25519-signed run ledger, one-time nonces, and a 15-minute authorization window

title: Sourcewarden
text: Evidence: Deterministic secret-detection policy blocks any self-improvement feedback containing a PEM key, named credential, or GitHub/OpenAI token pattern, fail closed

title: Sourcewarden
text: Evidence: FastAPI chat endpoint returns cited evidence for every answer, never a plan without a source

title: Sourcewarden
text: Evidence: Monitoring dashboard recomputes all security control hashes live against the signed manifest instead of trusting a cached result

title: Sourcewarden
text: Evidence: 71 tests across three offline suites (20 web layer, 34 retrieval, 17 self-improvement adversarial), run with no network and no vector database

title: Sourcewarden
text: Evidence: Ships as a single Docker image and degrades to a clear empty state instead of failing when the retrieval index isn't mounted

title: Sourcewarden
text: Architecture: Query -> FastAPI /chat -> retriever (router -> vector store -> rerank) over the retrieval index -> cited evidence back to the browser. Separately, /dashboard reads self-improvement run status, eval and tuning artifacts, and the security control hash manifest live, recomputing every hash rather than trusting a cache.

title: Sourcewarden
text: Tradeoff: Read only dashboard vs a live agent driver. A driver would demo better, but it either duplicates the approval ledger in the browser or bypasses it, so read only won

title: Sourcewarden
text: Tradeoff: Recomputing every security hash on each dashboard load vs trusting a cache. Slower page load, but a cached match can go stale and lie

title: Sourcewarden
text: Tradeoff: Single Docker image with no baked in index vs bundling one. Keeps the image small and the index out of version control, at the cost of an empty state chat until it is mounted

title: Sourcewarden
text: Decision: Read-only web layer, not an agent driver. The six-role pipeline's whole design point is a human approving every mutation through a signed run ledger. A chatbox that shells out to run it directly would either rebuild that approval flow or bypass it, so the web layer only reads: retrieval and status, never execution.

title: Sourcewarden
text: Decision: Reimplemented the hash check in Python instead of shelling out. The existing hash generator is Node-only, write-capable, and maintainer-only. Giving a read-only backend any path to a write-capable script defeats the point of read-only, and reimplementing removes both the external binary dependency and the shell-injection surface. Tradeoff: Two implementations of the same hashing rule now have to agree, and the repo does not record what that duplication costs to maintain.

title: Sourcewarden
text: Decision: Self-improvement may propose, never apply. The tuner and the controls that authorise it share one local trust boundary, so a local apply command would let a compromised tuner change both the behaviour and the evidence for it. The loop terminates at an external integrator instead. Tradeoff: The loop cannot close. Every proposal sits permanently on hold, because the external signing infrastructure that would complete it does not exist in the repository.

title: Sourcewarden
text: Decision: Fail closed by default on the mutation gate. Until a pinned public key and a matching signed ledger exist, the hooks deny. A gate that defaults to allow is a gate that is off. Tradeoff: The system is unusable for live mutation out of the box, and there is no in-repo demonstration of a successful signed mutation to show that the path works.

title: Sourcewarden
text: Decision: Merged the two source repos before building anything on top. Two repos evolving in parallel meant two copies of the same evidence-precedence logic. One index, one manifest, one place for a security fix to actually land.

title: Sourcewarden
text: Metrics: Retrieval Index: 2,256 rows; Security Hashes: Verified live; Tests: 71 passing

title: Sourcewarden
text: Tags: FastAPI, RAG, n8n, Security, Ed25519, Docker, Python. Status: SHIPPED.

title: MetaLearnML
text: MetaLearnML: Meta-Learned AutoML Ranking, Measured Against Its Baselines. I built an AutoML ranker, then the benchmark that proved it does not save time, and I kept that result. MetaLearnML is a tabular AutoML engine that ranks preprocessing by model candidates with a meta learner trained on past runs, next to a benchmark over 15 datasets built to measure whether that learned ranking actually beats proxy and random baselines. On end to end evaluation savings it does not, and the repo records that.

title: MetaLearnML
text: Problem: An AutoML system can rank candidate pipelines with a meta-learner trained on past runs, and the obvious claim is that better ranking finds a good pipeline in fewer evaluations. That claim is rarely tested against the baselines it needs to beat. This project builds the ranker and then builds the benchmark that decides whether the ranking actually saves any evaluations.

title: MetaLearnML
text: Constraint: Leakage. Development and test partitions split before any encoder is fitted, preprocessing fitted inside each fold, and the target dataset excluded from its own meta-training history.

title: MetaLearnML
text: Constraint: Cold start. Meta-ranking needs at least 20 compatible history rows before it can rank anything at all.

title: MetaLearnML
text: Constraint: Compute. CPU only on a single laptop, which bounds the candidate universe and the number of seeds.

title: MetaLearnML
text: Constraint: Licensing. Third-party datasets cannot be committed, so the suite is pinned by task version, checksum, and snapshot hash instead.

title: MetaLearnML
text: Constraint: The comparison is scoped. Exhaustive search is the reference inside a fixed 28 to 36 pipeline universe, not a global optimum.

title: MetaLearnML
text: Failure mode: The headline result is null and stays published. Median evaluation reduction against random is 0.0%, with a dataset-bootstrap 95% CI spanning 0% to 50% over 10,000 resamples, which does not establish a reduction. The repo states it does not claim a search speedup.

title: MetaLearnML
text: Failure mode: Ranking quality and evaluation savings came apart. Median Spearman is 0.5676 for meta-only against 0.0216 for random, so the learned ranking genuinely orders candidates better; it just does not convert that into fewer evaluations. The gap between those two facts is the actual finding.

title: MetaLearnML
text: Failure mode: One dataset visibly regresses and is published anyway: micro-mass at 0.154 test regret in a table where the rest are near zero. Another has negative R² for every method, meaning worse than predicting the mean.

title: MetaLearnML
text: Failure mode: 18 candidate runs failed on power transformation and are retained in the denominators rather than dropped, which depresses the method's own numbers.

title: MetaLearnML
text: Failure mode: No runtime or memory claim is made, because the cold wall-clock trial was not run and peak memory was not isolated. The published runtime plot is replay-equivalent, not wall clock.

title: MetaLearnML
text: Failure mode: The published evidence run was made from a dirty working tree, recorded in the report rather than hidden.

title: MetaLearnML
text: Evidence: Candidate universe: up to 12 preprocessing strategies × 7 (classification) or 9 (regression) models, ranked by fast proxy evaluation plus an optional RandomForest meta-learner over prior-run meta-features

title: MetaLearnML
text: Evidence: Leakage controls: outer dev/test split before any encoder is fit, fold-local preprocessing, a single scored touch of the test partition, deterministic splits, SHA-256 content-addressed candidate identity, and a versioned meta-feature schema that refuses to load on drift

title: MetaLearnML
text: Evidence: Benchmark: 15 OpenML datasets (8 classification, 7 regression), outer seeds [13, 42, 97], 5 inner folds, 20 seeded candidate orderings, methods {exhaustive, proxy, meta, proxy+meta, random}

title: MetaLearnML
text: Evidence: Ranking quality, meta vs random: median Spearman 0.57 vs 0.02, Recall@5 0.40 vs 0.20

title: MetaLearnML
text: Evidence: End-to-end: proxy+meta held 100% median quality retention at a budget of 10 candidates with 0.0 median normalized regret, but the median evaluation reduction vs random was 0.0% (95% CI 0.0% to 50.0%)

title: MetaLearnML
text: Evidence: 86 tests, Ruff-clean, GitHub Actions CI

title: MetaLearnML
text: Evidence: Optional FastAPI read API and Neo4j experiment-graph logging, kept as optional infrastructure rather than load-bearing claims

title: MetaLearnML
text: Architecture: CSV + label → task inference → candidate universe (preprocessing × model) → proxy score + meta-learner rank → fold-local CV on top-k → refit winner on all dev rows → single test score → deployable bundle + benchmark report

title: MetaLearnML
text: Tradeoff: Meta-learner vs proxy-only ranking: the meta-learner ranks better, but did not convert that into fewer end-to-end evaluations in the measured suite

title: MetaLearnML
text: Tradeoff: Report the null result vs bury it: the benchmark explicitly records that the speedup criterion was not met, so the claim cannot drift upward later

title: MetaLearnML
text: Tradeoff: Fixed 15-dataset suite vs broader coverage: a locked suite with committed result rows is reproducible; generalization beyond it is not claimed

title: MetaLearnML
text: Tradeoff: RandomForest over meta-features vs gradient-based meta-learning: a small inspectable regressor was enough to test the hypothesis and cheap to retrain

title: MetaLearnML
text: Decision: Build the benchmark that could disprove the engine. Meta-learned ranking is supposed to save evaluations. The only honest way to claim that is a leakage-resistant suite that measures it, including when the answer is no.

title: MetaLearnML
text: Decision: Pre-register the success bar in code, then publish the failure. The criterion is a boolean in the analysis script, evaluated automatically: a wholly positive bootstrap interval, at least 95% quality retention at budget 10, and regret no worse than 0.05. Deciding it after seeing results is how a null quietly becomes a win. Tradeoff: It cost the project its headline claim. The generator wrote 'resume impact criterion not met' and the machine-readable summary records eligibility as false.

title: MetaLearnML
text: Decision: Separate ranking quality from end-to-end savings. The meta-learner genuinely ranks better than random, by median Spearman 0.5676 against 0.0216. That is not the same as reaching a good model in fewer evaluations, and conflating the two is the trap. Tradeoff: Reporting both means publishing a real improvement next to a null result and refusing to let the first one stand in for the second.

title: MetaLearnML
text: Decision: Report replay-equivalent runtime instead of wall clock. Every ranking method replays the same measured candidates, folds and failures, which isolates ordering quality from execution noise. Tradeoff: It forfeits any speed claim outright: the cold end-to-end timing trial was never run, so the report cannot say the system is faster.

title: MetaLearnML
text: Decision: Content-address candidates and version the meta-feature schema. Reproducible identity and a schema that refuses to load on drift are what make a re-run comparable to the original.

title: MetaLearnML
text: Metrics: Ranking (meta vs random): 0.57 vs 0.02 ρ; Measured speedup: 0.0% (CI 0 to 50)

title: MetaLearnML
text: Tags: AutoML, scikit-learn, PyTorch, Meta-Learning, Benchmarking, Leakage Control, GitHub Actions CI. Status: SHIPPED.

title: ChatDB
text: ChatDB: Rule-Based Natural-Language-to-SQL CLI. Plain English questions into SQL with five regex rules and zero machine learning. ChatDB loads a CSV into SQLite and turns a fixed grammar of plain English aggregate questions into SQL with regex pattern matching, not a model.

title: ChatDB
text: Evidence: CSV ingestion with pandas: column-name normalization, then dtype-based classification into datetime / measure / attribute columns to drive query planning

title: ChatDB
text: Evidence: Five named regex intent patterns (sum / average / min / max / count, each grouped-by) mapped to SQL GROUP BY templates

title: ChatDB
text: Evidence: SQLAlchemy write-through into SQLite; the shipped CLI path prints the generated SQL rather than executing it

title: ChatDB
text: Evidence: Randomized sample-query generator so a new user sees the supported phrasing instead of guessing

title: ChatDB
text: Evidence: Exact, case-sensitive column matching with no fuzzy fallback; an unrecognized query returns an explicit error, never a wrong guess

title: ChatDB
text: Architecture: CSV → pandas load + column-type inference → SQLite via SQLAlchemy → NL query → regex intent match → SQL GROUP BY template → printed SQL

title: ChatDB
text: Tradeoff: Regex rules vs a parser or a model: rules are fully inspectable and need no training data, at the cost of covering only a fixed aggregate-by-group grammar

title: ChatDB
text: Tradeoff: Print the SQL vs execute it: printing keeps the tool a transparent translator and sidesteps unsafe interpolation in the shipped path

title: ChatDB
text: Tradeoff: Exact column matching vs fuzzy: exact matching fails loudly on a typo instead of silently querying the wrong column

title: ChatDB
text: Decision: Regex intent matching, no NLP. For a fixed grammar of aggregate-by-group questions, five readable patterns beat a parser you cannot debug and a model you cannot ship in a CLI.

title: ChatDB
text: Decision: Return an error on no match, never a guessed query. A natural-language-to-SQL tool that guesses is worse than one that says it does not understand. No match is an explicit failure, not a fallback.

title: ChatDB
text: Decision: Infer column roles from pandas dtypes at load time. Classifying columns as dates / measures / attributes once, up front, is what lets a short regex decide what can be summed and what can be grouped.

title: ChatDB
text: Metrics: Translation: 5 regex patterns; Stack: pandas · SQLAlchemy

title: jarvis
text: jarvis: Turn-Scoped Containment for Coding Agents. Once a coding agent reads something hostile, it stops being allowed to act for the rest of that turn. A Claude Code hook layer that screens tool results through Agent Shield, wraps flagged content as untrusted data before the model reads it, and denies every write, execute and network tool for the remainder of that turn, keyed by prompt_id.

title: jarvis
text: Evidence: Turn-scoped taint keyed by prompt_id, surviving across separate hook subprocesses, so ingest in one tool call constrains every later call in the same turn

title: jarvis
text: Evidence: Gate covers 14 tool names plus every mcp__* tool by prefix. The matcher was checked against the harness rather than assumed: a probe confirmed Bash and an MCP tool fire while Read does not, which a wildcard matcher would have hidden

title: jarvis
text: Evidence: Fails closed. With the screener pointed at a path that does not exist, a WebFetch was denied with an explicit reason rather than quietly allowed

title: jarvis
text: Evidence: Live deny rate of 1 denied in 10 gated calls, recorded with the allow path too, so the rate has a real denominator

title: jarvis
text: Evidence: 124 tests, and ten mutations reintroduced as defects were each observed red then restored byte-identical

title: jarvis
text: Evidence: Documents its own recall gaps rather than hiding them: as screened on 2026-09-17, secret-key assignments and a base64-piped-to-shell command scored allow low and are not wrapped. Those are gaps in the screener's ruleset, named in the README

title: jarvis
text: Architecture: Tool call → PostToolUse hook → Agent Shield screen → wrap flagged output as untrusted data and set turn taint → PreToolUse gate reads taint by prompt_id → deny writes, execution and network for the rest of the turn

title: jarvis
text: Tradeoff: PostToolUse cannot block, only rewrite, so quarantine wraps unconditionally when the guard is missing rather than pretending it screened something

title: jarvis
text: Tradeoff: Turn scope rather than session scope: a session-wide block would make one bad web page end the session, while a turn-scoped one degrades to read-only and recovers

title: jarvis
text: Tradeoff: Guards a cooperative model's mistakes, not an adversarial one. The run log is writable through Bash by means no gate here inspects, and the README says so rather than implying containment it does not provide

title: jarvis
text: Decision: Key the taint on prompt_id, not session_id. It is the only identifier that scopes to a single turn and survives across separate hook subprocesses. A probe confirmed a subagent's PreToolUse carries the parent turn's prompt_id, so taint propagates into subagents rather than leaking around them.

title: jarvis
text: Decision: Fail closed when the screener cannot run. A security layer that silently degrades to allow is worse than none, because it is trusted. An executable check denies writes and names the exact missing binary in the message.

title: jarvis
text: Decision: Publish the recall gaps in the README. The layer wraps what the screener flags, which is not the same as everything dangerous. Stating the payloads that currently score allow low is the difference between a security tool and a security claim.

title: jarvis
text: Metrics: Tests: 124; Mutations verified red: 10

title: jarvis
text: Tags: Claude Code Hooks, Prompt Injection, Taint Tracking, Fail-Closed, Python, Agent Shield. Status: SHIPPED.

title: Company Agents
text: Company Agents: An Executable Map of a Company's Roles. Company functions down to role agents, with a verifier that refuses to call a blank job done. An executable map of company functions to departments to branches to jobs to role agents, with a five-layer enforcement chain: job records, branch designs, a preflight gate, context screening through Agent Shield, and generated role agents.

title: Company Agents

text: Evidence: Three mutations reintroduced as defects, each observed red then restored

text: Evidence: Agent Shield wired in as a live dependency for context screening rather than named as a design intention

title: Company Agents
text: Architecture: Functions → departments → branches → job records → preflight gate → Agent Shield context screen → generated role agents, with a verifier over every layer

title: Company Agents
text: Tradeoff: Zero dependencies keeps the whole chain auditable and installable anywhere, at the cost of writing the runner and test scaffolding by hand

title: Company Agents
text: Tradeoff: Records and generated agents rather than hand-written agents: adding a company is configuration, but the generator becomes the thing that has to be right

title: Company Agents
text: Tradeoff: A preflight gate that fails on blank input costs runs that would previously have reported success, which is the point

title: Company Agents
text: Decision: A company is a pack plus a profile, not a fork. Forking the repo per company means every fix has to be applied N times and drift is guaranteed. Keeping the structure in records means a new company is data.

title: Company Agents
text: Decision: Fail the run on a blank job rather than let it exit 0. The failure that motivated this produced plausible output from empty inputs and reported success. An agent pipeline that cannot tell empty input from a hard task will confidently produce nothing.

title: Company Agents
text: Decision: Record what the repo is not. STATE.md carries the correction that this is not an operational multi-agent company, along with its open bugs. A skeleton described as a product is the failure mode this project exists to avoid.

title: Company Agents
text: Metrics: Verify steps: 42 / 42; Runtime deps: 0

id: publication/Beyond Attack Success Rate: Measuring Operator-Facing Transparency in LLM Agent Security
title: Beyond Attack Success Rate: Measuring Operator-Facing Transparency in LLM Agent Security
text: PREPRINT · ZENODO 2026: Beyond Attack Success Rate: Measuring Operator-Facing Transparency in LLM Agent Security. When an AI resists an attack but never mentions it, that's not the same as staying safe. I measure the difference. Sole-author preprint introducing a transparency-aware evaluation protocol on Inspect AI. Adds Transparency Rate (TR) as a third axis to the AgentDojo outcome matrix, with an anchored prompt-injection result (n=20, Wilson 95% CIs) across four models and diagnostic probes over six adversarial surfaces. Contribution: Transparency Rate; Harness: Inspect AI; Surfaces: 6 attack; Author: Sole author

title: About
text: I work on AI systems where model capability alone is not the hard part. The interesting questions sit around the model: what enters a limited context window, which tool call is safe to make, what the system does when retrieval misses, and how you would know any of it is working.

title: About
text: That pulls me toward evaluation. Most of my projects ship with the measurement attached, because a system I cannot re-run and get the same answer from is a demo, not a result. It also means I publish results that went against me: MetaLearnML's benchmark says its learned ranking does not reduce end to end evaluation time, and the repo records that rather than burying it.

title: About
text: I build across the stack it takes to get there, from adversarial evals and retrieval pipelines to FastAPI services, agent orchestration, and on-device computer vision. The domains change; the habit of instrumenting first does not.
